pillar_reactions.evidence: He pushed back on the substance of whether the training suits his body and his age group: "I've got a frozen elbow. You know, I can't even do half the stuff I want to do because I can't get my arm to go straight... I have some of those concerns that it may be premature for me." And on the evidence base: "I see a ton of guys in their 40s, but almost no testimonials from people that say, hey, I'm 55." He also questioned the credentialing behind it — "I have no idea what makes someone a kettlebell expert... Where do you get certified as a kettlebell expert?" — while explicitly saying he did not distrust Trevor.

Not delivered on this call. It came up only as a feature comparison — he noted the $200 membership "doesn't include the nutrition program", and during the screen share the rep described the Primal University nutrition protocol as "a basic one with an example of a meal plan".

The clearest pillar objection in the batch, and it is a pricing-of-accountability objection rather than a rejection of the idea: "If I had a guy sitting next to me and called me in the morning and woke me up and said, get your butt out of bed, let's go, and he was sitting next to me watching me the whole time, then I'd probably pay him $1,200. But to do a virtual program..." He values accountability highly and does not believe remote accountability is worth the same, drawing on his own experience — "I'd probably get a lot of it due to my experience my last time and just not having that."

anchors.raw: there's a guy here in town that will actually do a side-by-side for me for less than that... he does the nutritional program, he does all that
anchors.note: The decisive anchor. A local trainer offering in-person supervision plus nutrition for under $1,200 a month makes the remote premium indefensible in the prospect's framing, and he closed off the standard "you're not buying a PT" rebuttal himself by noting the local option covers nutrition and accountability too. The rep did not rebuild value on any other axis and effectively conceded.

anchors.raw: I have a gym membership. I can go get off my butt and go work out right now. That doesn't cost me anything.
anchors.note: The zero-cost fallback, and he half-endorsed it — "I know I wouldn't waste my time if I do some basic things." Note this is the inverse of his position on 11 June, where he framed the gym as something he hates. Under financial pressure the same asset flipped from a pain into an alternative.

anchors.raw: I'd probably never do an up front program like that, especially online. It's just my nature. My clients don't have to pay for my services up front. I earn them as I go.
anchors.note: He prices the offer against how he sells his own professional services, which makes upfront payment a matter of principle rather than cash flow. Any structure that requires payment before value is delivered will read as wrong to this buyer regardless of the amount, which is why the $1,200 trial failed as well as the $6,000.

anchors.raw: just three months ago, I literally had a half a million dollars just sitting in the bank... All that money is gone. It all went to save my marriage and my house... today I talked, and we just added another $27,000 onto the bill
anchors.note: Materially worse than what was disclosed on 11 June, where it read as a liquidity timing issue. This is a genuinely distressed household position that no payment structure reaches, and the rep was right to stop selling into it.

anchors.raw: when I was 35 and 38, I went and did CrossFit, I lost 30 pounds, I got immensely stronger, and I did it in two months. In two months, I dropped from, like, 18% body fat down to 12% body fat.
anchors.note: He has achieved a dramatic result before, quickly, at a gym-membership price point. That sets a very high bar for what $6,000 must deliver and it went unaddressed — the obvious counter, that the same approach later gave him rhabdomyolysis at 49, was available from the 11 June call and never used.

unmet_demand.want: Outcome evidence for men over 50 — testimonials, completion numbers, average starting and ending stats, and a conversation with a past client his age
unmet_demand.why_unmet: No such asset was offered and the questions were not answered. References are declined on policy — "we don't share our clients' numbers" — and testimonial participation is voluntary. Whether the underlying data exists is unknown from this call, which is exactly why it needs a human to check.

unmet_demand.want: An explanation of the written 10% body fat guarantee and how body fat would be measured
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The prospect quoted a guarantee he had read — "On some of the guarantees, it says 10% body fat loss. What does that mean?" — and the rep answered about the eight-kilo kettlebell guarantee instead. The follow-up "how do you guys measure body fat?" was never answered. The claim presumably means something; nobody on the call could say what.

unmet_demand.want: In-person, hands-on coaching with live form correction
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Structurally impossible in a remote model and the prospect can buy it locally for less. He is explicit that this is what accountability is worth paying for.

unmet_demand.want: A programme he and his wife can do together, adapted for a post-GLP-1 woman in her fifties
unmet_demand.why_unmet: There is no female offer. The answer given was that both should use the self-paced men's programme with the rep's own load adjustment: "she will definitely need to cut the weights at least half, probably, what he's proposing." That is improvised guidance for someone who is not a client and has never been assessed.

unmet_demand.want: To pay as value is delivered rather than in advance
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Every structure offered — $6,000 upfront, $1,200 for a month in advance, $200 a month in advance — requires payment before delivery. He runs his own practice the opposite way and treats it as a matter of principle.

unmet_demand.want: The full six-month plan visible up front so he can see what he is buying
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Partly served and partly deflected. The rep said the plan lives in the app but must stay adaptable — "you need to know that the program may change" — and the prospect accepted a semi-detailed version would satisfy him. Nothing was actually shown for the coached product.
